title: State renaming preserves computation
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $w$ be a Boolean input word, and let $tm$ and $host$ be machines with $k$ work tapes over Booleans. Suppose $emb:S\to H$ is a state map such that, for every state and every input and work-tape symbol tuple, the transition of $host$ at the embedded state is the state-renaming of the transition of $tm$. Then for every configuration $c$ and every natural number $t$, running $host$ from the configuration obtained by renaming the state of $c$ for $t$ steps gives the state-renaming of the configuration reached by running $tm$ from $c$ for $t$ steps.
